sentences.text: I would tell you if I had to.

sentences.text: He would help you if you asked him.

categories.label: This / That
categories.note: English demonstratives change only for number, not case.

categories.label: Possessive
categories.note: Determiner before a noun (my car); pronoun on its own (it's mine).

categories.label: Reflexive
categories.note: Subject and object are the same person; also for emphasis (I did it myself).

categories.label: Questions
categories.note: who (subject), whom (object / after a preposition), whose (possessive). 'what' never changes.

sentences.text: To whom did you give it?

categories.label: Relative
categories.note: who/whom for people, which for things, that for both, whose for possession. You can often drop it: 'the book I read'.

sentences.text: The man who lives here is my teacher.
The woman whom I met is a doctor.
The man whose car is new lives here.

patterns.subtitle: relative pronoun for things

sentences.text: The book which I read was good.
The house that we bought is old.
The film, which won a prize, is long.

patterns.note: You can usually drop it: 'the book I read'.

categories.label: Indefinite
categories.note: Pronouns for unspecified people/things. Use some- in statements, any- in questions/negatives.

categories.label: Prepositions + it
categories.note: English has no 'da-words' — use a preposition + it/them, or put the preposition at the end.

patterns.subtitle: things after a preposition
patterns.note: For things use it/them; questions often end with the preposition.
